meta.title: Business Technology Consulting
meta.one_liner: How consultants think, how they interview, and how technology projects get built and managed.
meta.blurb: I built this course for CMU Qatar from an older systems analysis and design course, and turned it toward both sides of consulting: the business analysis that consulting firms hire for, and the technology work of designing and running a project. The first half was frameworks and case interviews, with Harvard cases on Deloitte and BCG and live practice cases like Harley-Davidson and a fighter jet division. The second half ran a Harvard change management simulation and then moved into the systems development life cycle, UML, agile, and project management. Students in Business Administration, Information Systems, and Computer Science took it together, and it was built to get them ready for a first-round interview at firms like McKinsey, BCG, Accenture, and Bain.

assignments.name: Case interviews
assignments.description: In 2015, each student prepared two interview scripts, ran four case interviews with a partner (two as interviewer, two as candidate), and wrote a three to five page analysis of strengths and improvements for each. A second round followed with a new partner, then a case interview and a behavioral interview with me.

assignments.name: Client project
assignments.description: Teams in 2015 worked through a full engagement for a client inside the university: a client interview graded against a rubric, a five to eight page proposal with a work breakdown structure and cost estimate at set daily rates, a technical design in UML, a user interface design, and a working prototype.

assignments.name: Final consulting project
assignments.description: In 2014, small groups chose a real organization and applied the course frameworks (profit, business situation, SWOT, Porter) to a problem it faced, presented during the final exam period.

assignments.name: Simulations
assignments.description: Harvard's change management simulation, run once in a low-urgency and once in a high-urgency scenario, plus project management and strategy simulations in 2015.

assignments.name: Exams
assignments.description: Closed-book exams, one-third short answer and two-thirds consulting case analysis. In 2014 the midterm and final were 30% and 40%; in 2015 a single final was 20%.

items.subject: Vodafone Qatar
items.approach: Porter's five forces and a youth-market strategy
items.description: Looked at Vodafone's launch of Falla, the first Qatari telecom plan aimed at young people, and asked which youth products and services Vodafone should focus on to position itself against Ooredoo.

items.subject: Zara
items.description: Analyzed Zara's vertically integrated, fast-turnover model, including its single distribution center and weak online presence, and recommended where it should grow next.

items.subject: A GCC charity supporting Syrian refugees
items.approach: Profit framework, SWOT, and business situation framework
items.description: The charity raised most of its money through events, an unstable source. The team estimated its revenues and costs and recommended ways to increase donations and build a steadier income.

items.subject: A yoga studio in Doha
items.approach: SWOT, competitive comparison, BCG matrix, and Porter's five forces
items.description: Asked how the studio could grow with the market, cross-sell, and attract new customers, and recommended partnerships with sports and hotel facilities, corporate yoga, and better merchandising.

items.subject: A long-established Doha electronics and video game retailer
items.approach: Profit analysis from interviews with the general manager and an accountant
items.description: Compared revenue and costs from 2011 to 2012, and weighed small stores, limited capital, and the shift to digital games against the store's reputation and locations.

items.subject: Visualizing Twitter for academic assessment
items.approach: Client interview, proposal, UML design, UI design, prototype
items.description: A tool to pull a Twitter stream by search term, sort it into threads, and let an instructor grade students' contributions to discussion outside class.

items.subject: Digitizing negotiation exercises
items.approach: Client interview, proposal, UML design, UI design, prototype
items.description: A web platform, aimed at the iPad, for running classroom negotiation exercises like New Recruit so that results and scoring are immediate instead of done on paper.
